works.title: The Last of Us Part II — Academic Research Project
works.abstract: This project conducts a comprehensive, interdisciplinary academic investigation of Naughty Dog's *The Last of Us Part II* (2020). Moving beyond conventional reviews and plot summaries, this research examines how the game constructs characters, manipulates perspective and information distribution, structures trauma and grief, de-optionalizes interactive violence, and destabilizes player moral agency.

works.title: Digitally Cancelled? Social Media, Preference Falsification, and the Failure of the Internet Blackout in Bangladesh's July 2024 Uprising
works.abstract: Theoretical and empirical analysis proposing the construct of digital cancellation and a five-mechanism (CASED) model for platform-mediated legitimacy collapse during Bangladesh's July 2024 uprising. Includes a 31-column Phase 3 empirical rumour corpus (N = 141) and a 76-day day-level telecommunications measurement panel (OONI, IODA).

works.title: Metro: Last Light — Academic Research Project
works.abstract: This repository contains an exhaustive, interdisciplinary academic research study investigating *Metro: Last Light*. Rather than a conventional review or plot retrospective, this project investigates the game as an interactive narrative regarding humanity's survival after nuclear catastrophe and its persistent reproduction of the ideological, political, and moral conflicts that precipitated destruction.
